description: Removes the redundant but from sentence-initial although/even though ... , but ... surfaces.
fp_risk_note: Low risk. V1 only removes the redundant but in sentence-initial although / even though ... , but ... surfaces and leaves standalone although/even though clauses unchanged.

positive.input: Although I was tired, but I went home.
positive.expectedCorrection: Although I was tired, I went home.
positive.notes: Sentence-initial although-clause with redundant but; but is removed.

positive.input: Even though it was late, but we stayed.
positive.expectedCorrection: Even though it was late, we stayed.

positive.input: Although he was busy, but he helped me.
positive.expectedCorrection: Although he was busy, he helped me.
positive.notes: Redundant but after a causal although-clause.

positive.input: Even though I was hungry, but I waited.
positive.expectedCorrection: Even though I was hungry, I waited.

negative.input: Although I was tired, I went home.
negative.expectedCorrection: Although I was tired, I went home.
negative.notes: Standalone although-clause with no redundant but must stay unchanged.

negative.input: I was tired, but I went home.
negative.expectedCorrection: I was tired, but I went home.
negative.notes: Standalone but-result clause must stay unchanged.

negative.input: Even though I was tired, I went home.
negative.expectedCorrection: Even though I was tired, I went home.
negative.notes: Already-correct even though clause must stay unchanged.

negative.input: I stayed home although I was tired.
negative.expectedCorrection: I stayed home although I was tired.
negative.notes: Mid-sentence although-clause is not this rule.

negative.input: Although it rained, I went out, but I came home early.
negative.expectedCorrection: Although it rained, I went out, but I came home early.
negative.notes: Trickiest over-fire boundary: an although-clause followed by a separate, legitimate but-coordination. The but here is a real second clause coordinator (went out / came home early), not the redundant although...but pairing. The redundant-pairing surface requires but immediately after the first comma; here it does not, so the rule must abstain.
